title: Add the combined engine and client install mode
summary: The Forgel Code installer, run with no extra flags, installs the engine alongside the client, so the documented one-command install yields a working pair. It is idempotent by comparing the installed engine against the version the configured engine source provides: no engine installs it, an installed engine at or above the available one is kept untouched, a strictly newer available engine replaces it, and the finished result always satisfies the declared minimum, failing with an actionable message when it cannot. The default engine source is a documented configuration, and the run reports which engine version is installed.
requirements: The change set contains no automated check that reads documentation text.
The helper data that reproduced the documented installation text is gone, so no automated check can compare the instructions against a stored copy.
The check that previously read the installation instructions no longer exists and no replacement check of documentation text is introduced in its place.
Every other automated check remains present, its premise is unchanged, and none is removed or weakened by this change.
The installer and the client keep their previous behaviour: this change alters no program behaviour outside the wording of the installation instructions.
The installation instructions state, as text, that the single documented command installs the client together with an engine the client supports, so the result is a working pair.
The installation instructions name the default engine source and state how a run can be pointed at another source.
The installation instructions describe the client-only installation option and state that it leaves any engine untouched.
The installation instructions state that a successful run reports which engine version is in place and how it was obtained.
The installation instructions no longer present an already installed engine as a precondition the owner must satisfy before running the documented command.
The installation instructions are accepted or returned only by reviewing their text.

constraints: Documentation is text in this project: it is accepted or returned by reading it, and never by an automated check.
The removal must be surgical: only the documentation-reading check and the helper data that reproduced the documented text go; everything else stays.
No behavioural guarantee may be traded for the removal: a failing or weakened neighbouring check is a failure of this change.
The instructions must stay consistent with what an installation run actually does, since a person, not a machine, now catches a divergence.
Only the change set belonging to this task is part of it; unrelated files are left alone.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.
